summary: Seven experiments completed in 1.2 minutes, including two compute-bound tasks. The 0.97-minute synthesis-only freshness receipt was the largest recorded item; the longest named compute-bound item took 0.16 minutes, and the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle flag is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Freshness-receipt synthesis concentrated most of the observed wall time.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides no phase breakdown, so the cause of the longest named compute-bound duration cannot be determined.
The supplied records do not identify the other compute-bound task or state whether any task loaded multiple models concurrently, leaving runner-selection efficiency unmeasured.
improvements_suggested: Make the freshness receipt content-addressed and incremental so unchanged literature and implementation inputs reuse prior receipts.
Persist monotonic phase timings in every experiment artifact instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Record task-time GPU samples and declared model concurrency; choose DualGPURunner only when multiple models are actually loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add change detection and receipt caching to the freshness scan.
Emit phase-level start, stop, and elapsed timing with each experiment result.
Capture model concurrency and task-correlated GPU telemetry for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports optimizing the synthesis receipt and improving observability, but it does not supply a measured faster-path counterfactual, so no nonzero savings metric is asserted. The idle GPU snapshot is not attributed to compute execution because the locked task-conditioned field is false.
